payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery designed to reduce electrolyte crossover and aging. Independent testing corrected the initial claim: the governing cycle life is 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold, while the earlier 12,000-cycle figure was retracted because it used an un-normalized depth of discharge. The prototype’s gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. Projected stack-level cost is $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. The chemistry has an operating-temperature floor of 4 °C, below which the thalliline dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.
